challenge.title: Value-Based Healthcare depends on what happens between appointments.
challenge.body: Chronic conditions are managed every day, but clinicians see patients at intervals. Between visits, changes in symptoms, medication use, self-management and quality of life can remain invisible until the next appointment. That makes proactive care harder, consumes clinical time when teams try to fill the gap manually, and leaves providers without the continuous, longitudinal patient-reported data needed to measure outcomes and support Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC).

points.title: Follow-up does not scale manually
points.body: Clinical teams cannot personally call every patient often enough. As chronic-care cohorts grow, routine outreach competes with higher-value clinical work.

points.title: Important changes can surface late
points.body: Symptoms, missed medication, self-management difficulties and new concerns can develop between visits without reaching the care team until the next appointment.

points.title: Outcomes evidence remains incomplete
points.body: Patient-reported information from follow-up is often fragmented or unstructured, making it difficult to trend across a population, support clinical review, demonstrate outcomes and contribute to Value-Based Healthcare.

how.title: One continuous follow-up loop — before, between and after appointments.
how.subtitle: Haali reaches patients by phone, gathers the information relevant to their pathway, structures what they report, and puts the right evidence in front of the clinical team for review.

steps.name: Pre-Appointment Check-In
steps.title: Collect the information clinicians need before the patient arrives.
steps.body: Before a first appointment or follow-up visit, Haali can call the patient in their preferred language and gather pathway-relevant information such as symptoms, medication use, recent changes and patient concerns. The result is a structured pre-visit summary for clinical review, so the consultation can start with more of the patient story already available.
bullets: Natural conversation in Arabic and English
Pathway-based collection of symptoms, medication use and patient concerns
Structured pre-visit summary with the original conversation available as supporting evidence

steps.name: Haali Voice
steps.title: Stay connected to patients between appointments without adding routine calling workload.
steps.body: At configured intervals, Haali conducts natural follow-up conversations to understand how the patient is doing, clarify relevant responses, capture medication adherence and patient-reported concerns, and flag issues that require clinical attention. In-scope general education can be answered using approved clinical content; personal treatment or diagnosis questions are handed back to the clinical team.
bullets: General patient education restricted to approved clinical content
Questions adapted to the patient's condition, treatment and follow-up needs
Extends follow-up coverage without increasing routine clinical workload proportionally

steps.name: Clinical Review & Outcomes
steps.title: Turn every follow-up conversation into structured clinical information and longitudinal outcomes.
steps.body: Haali converts patient conversations into reviewable summaries, structured findings, patient-reported outcome measures and coding suggestions, with the original conversation available as supporting evidence. Clinicians validate what matters, while longitudinal data can be trended across patients and cohorts to support service improvement, outcomes measurement and Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC).
bullets: Evidence-linked summaries, structured findings and coding suggestions for clinician review
PROMs and pathway measures captured as structured, trendable data
Executive analytics to support outcomes measurement and Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC)

clinicalAi.title: AI that supports clinical teams — without taking clinical decisions away from them.
clinicalAi.subtitle: Haali uses AI to conduct natural patient conversations, clarify responses, structure what patients report and highlight information that may need attention. Clinical decisions remain with authorised healthcare professionals.

cards.title: Natural conversation, controlled clinical scope
cards.body: Haali can speak naturally with patients while following the clinical pathway configured for that follow-up. The conversation can adapt to what the patient says without becoming an unrestricted medical chatbot.

cards.title: Approved clinical knowledge
cards.body: When patients ask in-scope health questions, Haali uses approved clinical content rather than relying on unrestricted general model knowledge. If the approved information is not sufficient, Haali does not improvise a clinical answer.

cards.title: Safety before workflow
cards.body: Patient responses are continuously assessed against configured safety rules. When a relevant concern is identified, routine questioning can be interrupted and the case highlighted for the appropriate clinical review or escalation pathway.

cards.title: Evidence behind every finding
cards.body: AI-generated summaries and structured findings remain linked to the underlying patient conversation. Clinicians can review the original transcript, translation where required, supporting evidence and terminology suggestions before accepting anything into the clinical record.

cards.title: Clinicians remain in control
cards.body: Haali can suggest structured findings and medical terminology, but clinicians review, accept, correct or reject those suggestions. Haali does not independently diagnose patients, prescribe treatment or change medication.

clinicalAi.flowTitle: From conversation to reusable clinical data
flow: Approved information becomes reusable clinical data
cannot: Tell patients to start or stop medicines

cards.title: Clinical capacity released
cards.body: Routine follow-up, information gathering and documentation can be shifted away from repeated manual calls, giving clinical teams more time for review, intervention and direct care.

cards.title: Earlier visibility between visits
cards.body: Regular follow-up can surface new symptoms, medication issues and patient concerns between appointments, so the clinical team has information sooner than it would through episodic care alone.

cards.title: Low-friction patient reach
cards.body: Patients answer a normal phone call and speak naturally in Arabic or English, with no app, portal account or new digital behaviour required.

cards.title: Clinical review prioritised
cards.body: Haali structures what the patient reports and highlights calls that need attention, helping clinical teams review the right patients first instead of reading every conversation from the beginning.

cards.title: Structured clinical intelligence
cards.body: Evidence-linked summaries, patient-reported findings, pathway measures and terminology suggestions turn conversations into information that can be reviewed, trended and reused.

cards.title: Longitudinal outcomes and executive insight
cards.body: Follow-up data can be trended across patients, pathways and cohorts to support service improvement, population oversight and Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC).

vbhc.title: Turn continuous follow-up into outcomes intelligence.
vbhc.subtitle: Haali transforms patient follow-up into structured, longitudinal information that healthcare leaders can analyse across patients, pathways and populations. See who is being reached, where clinical review is needed, how patient-reported and pathway measures are changing, and what follow-up activity means for clinical capacity — creating a stronger information foundation for service improvement and Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC).

cards.title: Population Visibility
cards.headline: Understand what is happening between appointments.
cards.body: See follow-up coverage, patient engagement, emerging concerns and clinical-review demand across defined cohorts and pathways.

cards.title: Outcomes Visibility
cards.headline: Follow change over time, not just individual encounters.
cards.body: Trend patient-reported measures, pathway indicators, clinical review activity and other agreed outcomes at patient, cohort and service level.

cards.title: Operational Value
cards.headline: Understand the resources behind follow-up.
cards.body: Measure activity and clinical-review demand, then combine Haali data with agreed provider assumptions or connected data to model capacity, cost and programme value.

closing.title: Supporting Value-Based Healthcare
closing.body: Value-Based Healthcare requires providers to understand outcomes across patient populations alongside the resources used to deliver care. Haali helps create the longitudinal information layer needed to support that measurement — connecting what patients report between appointments with clinical review, pathway performance and population-level insight.

security.title: Designed for secure healthcare deployment from day one.
security.subtitle: Haali is being built with healthcare-grade access control, encryption, auditability and deployment flexibility in mind. Production security controls, hosting location and compliance requirements are confirmed with each provider before real patient deployment.
security.regionalNote: Saudi-first. Designed for country-specific privacy, health-data and cybersecurity requirements across the GCC.
security.safeguardsTitle: How the platform is being built

safeguards.title: Encryption by design
safeguards.body: Patient data is designed to be protected in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption in production deployments.

safeguards.title: Deployment-aligned data location
safeguards.body: Hosting and processing architecture can be configured around the provider's regulatory, contractual and data-location requirements.

safeguards.title: Role-based access
safeguards.body: Doctor, Care Coordinator and administrative permissions are separated so users only access the functions and information relevant to their role.

safeguards.title: Auditability and traceability
safeguards.body: Key user actions, AI outputs, clinician review decisions and configuration versions are designed to be recorded for review and governance.

security.roadmapNote: Haali is at an early deployment stage. Formal compliance, security assurance and certification activities will be completed in line with production deployment requirements. We will distinguish clearly between controls that are implemented, assessments that are underway and certifications that have been formally achieved.

roadmap.name: Saudi regulatory readiness
roadmap.scope: PDPL and applicable NCA cybersecurity, cloud and data controls assessed for each production deployment.

roadmap.name: GCC regulatory readiness
roadmap.scope: Architecture designed to be assessed against each country's privacy, health-data, hosting and cybersecurity requirements before deployment.

roadmap.name: ISO/IEC 27001 · 27701
roadmap.scope: Information Security Management and Privacy Information Management certification planned as the organisation and privacy programme mature.

roadmap.name: Digital health regulatory readiness
roadmap.scope: Haali's intended use and regulatory classification will be assessed for each market as the platform progresses from controlled pilots to clinical deployment.

alignment: ISO 27799 — healthcare information-security controls informing Haali's health-data security design.
ISO/IEC 27017 / 27018 — cloud security and cloud privacy controls informing hosting and processor due diligence.

Saudi-first, country-specific authorisation — Saudi/SFDA requirements assessed first, followed by the applicable national requirements for the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman as commercial deployment expands.
security.integrationTitle: Designed to fit into your existing HIS / EHR ecosystem
security.integrationBody: Haali is designed to sit alongside the clinical systems your teams already use. Patient follow-up produces structured, clinician-reviewed information that can be exported or integrated into existing workflows using standards-based interfaces. Integration scope is configured with each provider, including FHIR/HL7, APIs and NPHIES-aligned exchange where applicable.

integrations.label: REST APIs & webhooks — configured per deployment

security.note: Integration architecture, data flows, security controls and deployment requirements are confirmed with each provider during technical due diligence.
